study: Did renewables actually displace fossil power? (2000-2022, 187 countries, Our World in Data)
method: Every claim in report.html / manuscript.pdf is backed by a result in results.json (computed by src/analysis.py) or a verified literature source below. No citation, DOI, page number, or data value is invented.

claims.claim: Global renewable electricity share rose 18.6% -> 31% of generation (2000->2022)
Fossil generation rose +7,861 TWh even as renewables rose +8,495 TWh; only 31% of countries cut fossil
Holding country+year fixed, +1pp renewable share ~ -0.61% CO2/capita (p<0.001), stable under clustered SE, lag, first-difference
Effect largest in Europe (-0.53%/pp) and Americas (-0.76%/pp); smallest/insignificant in Africa & Asia
Grid carbon intensity falls ~0.7% per +1pp renewable share (mechanism check)
At constant momentum, fossil generation rises to ~19,345 TWh by 2030 (still growing)
To hold fossil flat by 2030 needs ~49.5% low-carbon share (momentum only ~44.5%)
Decoupling (intensity) is real and spreading; displacement (generation) is not yet happening in aggregate
